before.rappels: About 5-6 rappels from bolted anchors if you descend the ridge line: the first station is obvious just west of the summit, two rappels bring you down to a flat part of the ridge, then the line is forced off the crest onto 3rd-class ledges on the south side, with three more bolted rappels to reach the ground. Some parties instead reverse the ridge with short downclimbs and occasional rappels, or descend the South Buttress's established rappel line.

days.note: Graded a Mountaineers 'basic' climb but airy and committing: a loose scree/choss approach leads to the Southwest Gully, then sustained class 3-4 climbing along a narrow, hugely exposed ridge crest with running belays. Shorter than the South Buttress but still a full single-day outing for most parties.
days.title: West Ridge, car-to-car

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Approach through forest and meadow to the base of the Southwest Gully.

schedule.label: Southwest Gully
schedule.detail: Two class 3-4 pitches gain the ridge crest through loose, choss-covered terrain.

schedule.label: Ridge traverse
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 scrambling along the narrow spine, including the exposed 'Humps' section, with running belays.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Most parties top out by early-to-mid afternoon.

schedule.label: Descend
schedule.detail: About 4 rappels off the west side plus scree/gully hiking back toward the trail.

days.objective: Climb the West Ridge and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A single day car-to-car, roughly 3.6 mi and ~3,300 ft round trip; trip reports range from about 10 to 13 hours depending on route-finding and rappel efficiency.

before.beta: Grade II, 5th-class climbing to about 5.6 (harder direct variations reach 5.7). Short approach from highway. Rock improves significantly higher on ridge. Fair granite in approach, improves on ridge. Moderate exposure. Quick alpine climb from Rainy Pass. Uncrowded route.

days.note: The 'Complete' South Buttress follows the full original line low on the buttress (published topos show up to 22 pitches) rather than the commonly-linked ~12-pitch version, making it a longer day of rope work than the standard South Buttress before the same long descent.
days.title: Complete South Buttress, car-to-car

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Forest and meadow approach to the base of the buttress.

schedule.label: Base of route
schedule.detail: Rack up for a full-length pitched ascent.

schedule.label: Climb
schedule.detail: Up to ~16 pitches of wandering moderate rock to 5.8, more sustained rope work than the standard linked-out version.

schedule.label: Descend
schedule.detail: Multi-rappel descent (West Ridge or reversing the buttress) then hike out.

days.objective: Climb the full South Buttress line (up to 22 pitches) and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A long single car-to-car day, roughly 4.0 mi and an estimated ~3,300 ft round trip; expect 11-14 hours given the extra pitches over the standard South Buttress line.

before.rappels: Single 60m rope; roughly 10-12 rappels down the buttress, generally following the line of ascent

before.overview: A modern, sustained 5.11 alpine testpiece up Cutthroat's East Face, with four bolt-protected headwall pitches (5.10-5.11) linking natural, less-traveled terrain below and above — a quality alternative to the crowded Liberty Bell group just to the south.
before.descent: Rappel the route (the four bolted headwall pitches allow a two-rope rappel), or descend via the South Buttress or West Ridge if other parties are on those routes.

days.note: The shortest and least committing of Cutthroat's technical lines: a quick approach leads to 2-3 short pitches gaining the North Ridge Notch, then mostly class 2-4 ridge climbing with one steeper 5.6-5.7 section before easing off near the top.
days.title: North Ridge, car-to-car

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Short, pleasant approach through forest/meadow to the base of the North Ridge Notch.

schedule.label: Gain the notch
schedule.detail: 2-3 short low-5th-class pitches to the North Ridge Notch.

schedule.label: Climb the ridge
schedule.detail: ~8 pitches, mostly 2nd-4th class ramps and corners with one steeper 5.6-5.7 slab section.

schedule.label: Descend
schedule.detail: Downclimb plus ~5 rappels via the West Ridge side back to the notch, then hike out.

days.objective: Climb the North Ridge (Grade II, 5.6-5.7, ~8 pitches) and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A shorter single-day outing than Cutthroat's other lines: roughly 4.0 mi and an estimated ~2,800 ft round trip, typically well under 10 hours.

before.overview: The North Ridge is a moderate, less-traveled alternative to the South Buttress: an 8-pitch, roughly 600-foot Grade II-III 5.7 ridge climb first done by Fred Beckey, Jim Crooks, and Ed Kenney on August 19, 1940.
